# Gifsync

> Gifsync is a free browser tool that retimes a GIF's frames so its animation lands on the
> beat of a song, then saves the result as an MP4 with the audio in it. It runs entirely in
> the page: the GIF and the song are never uploaded, there is no account, and there is no
> watermark.

It is not an "add music to a GIF" tool. Those lay an audio track under an animation and
leave the animation alone, so the loop slides out of time with the song. Gifsync changes
the animation instead: a GIF stores a duration per frame, so each pair of marked frames is
stretched to span exactly one beat and the loop closes on a beat.

Tempo is estimated with a TempoCNN model running in the page through TensorFlow.js, and
can be typed or tapped in instead. GIFs can be searched from Wikimedia Commons, which
states a licence for every file.

## Pages

- [Gifsync](https://p3zo.github.io/gifsync/): the tool, plus how it works and the common questions
- [Examples](https://p3zo.github.io/gifsync/examples/): one GIF and one song timed three ways, with sound
- [BPM to frame timing](https://p3zo.github.io/gifsync/bpm-frame-timing/): how long to hold each frame at a given tempo, and why a GIF cannot express it exactly
- [Match a GIF to your project tempo](https://p3zo.github.io/gifsync/for-producers/): for a tempo you already know from a DAW
- [Sync a GIF to an osu! beatmap's BPM](https://p3zo.github.io/gifsync/osu/)

## Source

- [github.com/p3zo/gifsync](https://github.com/p3zo/gifsync)
